sources_considered.why: Primary announcement dated September 17, 2024, reporting the 800-developer study.
Primary controlled experiment reporting substantial benefits on a bounded programming task.
The September 2024 paper also supports the comparison; assessed directly under the second claim.
Read to establish context, not used as evidence of correctness.

evidence_items.locator: Results, paragraph beginning “No significant change to efficiency metrics”

receipt.public_excerpt: Developers with Copilot did not see an increase in coding speed.

evidence_items.explanation: The published study reported no significant improvement in pull-request cycle time or throughput. Its results support the claim about the contemporary research record, although they cannot establish a universal absence of benefits.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Peng, Kalliamvakou, Cihon and Demirer
evidence_items.locator: Results, paragraph discussing Figure 6 and task-completion times

receipt.public_excerpt: This represents a 55.8% reduction in completion time.

evidence_items.explanation: This positive experiment found a substantial reduction in the time needed for one programming task, still well short of the 90% reduction corresponding to tenfold speed. It limits any suggestion that the evidence showed negligible benefits everywhere.

unresolved_gaps: These studies do not measure every programming activity or establish a population-wide productivity effect.
